newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The won closed lower versus the dollar on Monday as fewer-than-expected month-end export deals prompted banks to cover their dollar positions, traders said.
But continuous dollar inflow from depository receipt issue by Cho Hung Bank supported the local unit, they said.
The won finished at 829.60 after opening at a day high of 829.00. It touched a low of 829.90.
Traders said many bank had gone short in dollars on Friday, expecting large month-end export deals on Saturday. However, the size of export deals turned out to be smaller than expected, they said.
Dealers said Cho Hung Bank was waiting for the won to fall to around 830 so they can unload dollars from its $180 million global depository receipts (GDR) issue in London last week.
"Most banks are afraid to buy the dollar as Cho Hung is expected to unwind their dollar positions coming from the GDR issue," said one dealer.
Traders expected the won to trade between 829.00 to 830.50 on Tuesday. The central bank set the base mid-rate at 829.50 for Tuesday against 828.70 for Monday.
